newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DIW says German domestic demand still lags.
newsitem.headline: German DIW says German domestic demand still lags.

text.p: Germany's DIW economic institute said on Wednesday that it expected real German GDP to rise 0.5 percent in the third quarter of 1997 from the second quarter, and to be two percent above the year-ago period.
But incoming order data showed that the lively demand from abroad was not yet stimulating domestic demand, the DIW said in a report on the first six months of 1997.
"It is above all dependent on foreign business at what pace overall German production will expand," the institute said.

DIW calculations showed real German gross domestic product (GDP) grew by 2.7 percent in the second quarter from the first quarter, giving a growth rate of around two percent for the first six months as a whole.
However the DIW said the data were distorted because the second quarter had more working days than the first quarter and that real adjusted growth had been only about one percent.
"Probably the pace of developments in overall economic production in Germany in both quarters actually differed only marginally," the report said.
The institute had said in July that it expected German economic growth of two percent in 1997 and 1998.
